note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following confirmed prostate cancer with rising PSA levels.

Recently retired secondary school teacher, now 73 years old, presents for re-evaluation of known prostate cancer. He has a history of chronic kidney disease and osteoarthritis, managed with paracetamol as needed. His PSA has steadily increased from 4.2 ng/mL in September 2022 to 14.5 ng/mL in February 2025. He is married, lives with his partner, and has a long-time friend as his next of kin. He consumes approximately 9 units of alcohol per week and leads a sedentary lifestyle with occasional walking. He has mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 1/35. He is currently attending the sleep clinic for suspected obstructive sleep apnoea. He lives more than 90 minutes from the clinic and prefers phone follow-up where clinically safe.

On digital rectal examination, a nodule is palpated in the prostate gland, consistent with clinical stage cT2a. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs, blood pressure 114/71 mmHg, and heart rate 70 bpm. No signs of acute distress or metastatic disease are noted.
